summary: This article explains how animation creates the illusion of movement from many still pictures shown quickly, from hand-drawn frames to modern computer animation, and the teamwork it takes to make an animated film.
introduce: Write First, Next, Then, and Finally on the board and ask a volunteer to use them to describe how they get ready for school. Tell students to watch for the order of events as they read “Animation: Bringing Drawings to Life”.

keyTerms.def: a person whose job is to create the drawings or models that make a character move
one single picture in a moving film
something that looks real or true but is not

challengeTerms.def: to use a computer to turn a plain 3D model into a finished, colored picture
a digital skeleton of movable joints inside a 3D character model, used to pose and move it
to match two things so they happen at exactly the same time

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that making an animated movie is harder than drawing one picture? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain what a storyboard is and why a studio makes one before drawing the finished pictures for a movie.
struggling: Pre-teach animator, frame, and illusion with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers put sentence strips of the main events in order before writing.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses render, rig, and synchronize to summarize the key events in order and explain which step matters most.
